rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM music_Track;

WITH counts AS (SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS album_count FROM music_Artist ar JOIN music_Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name) SELECT Name, album_count FROM counts WHERE album_count = (SELECT MAX(album_count) FROM counts);
SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM music_Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY customer_count DESC, Country;
rows.note: I'm counting rows in `music_Customer` grouped by `Country`.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS total_revenue FROM music_Invoice GROUP BY year ORDER BY year;
rows.note: Assuming "invoice revenue" means the sum of Total from music_Invoice grouped by calendar year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS full_name, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS total_spent FROM music_Customer c JOIN music_Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 5

WITH counts AS (SELECT SupportRepId, COUNT(*) AS n FROM music_Customer WHERE SupportRepId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SupportRepId) SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, counts.n AS customers FROM counts JOIN music_Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = counts.SupportRepId WHERE counts.n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM counts);
SELECT COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS track_count FROM music_Playlist p JOIN music_PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge';
SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_purchased_tracks FROM music_Track WHERE TrackId NOT IN (SELECT TrackId FROM music_InvoiceLine WHERE TrackId IS NOT NULL);
SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS Revenue FROM music_Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'm treating revenue as the sum of `Total` from `music_Invoice` for invoices dated in 2012, grouped by `BillingCountry`.

rows.sql:
SELECT ar.Name AS ArtistName
FROM music_Artist ar
JOIN music_Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
JOIN music_Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3;

SELECT g.Name AS genre,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM music_InvoiceLine), 2) AS percentage
FROM music_InvoiceLine il
JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
LEFT JOIN music_Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.Name
ORDER BY percentage DESC;
rows.note: Assuming revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity from InvoiceLine, grouped by track genre, with the percentage taken over all invoice lines.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM music_Invoice i
JOIN music_InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN music_Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
  AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
    SELECT i2.CustomerId
    FROM music_Invoice i2
    JOIN music_InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
    JOIN music_Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
    JOIN music_Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
    WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
  );
rows.note: I'm assuming genre names are exactly 'Rock' and 'Jazz', and that a customer's purchases are traced through invoices, invoice lines and tracks.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM music_Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM music_Employee e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM music_Customer c WHERE c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId) ORDER BY e.EmployeeId LIMIT 50;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010 FROM (SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_purchase FROM music_Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) WHERE strftime('%Y', first_purchase) = '2010'

SELECT a.Title, ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 1) AS minutes FROM music_Album a JOIN music_Track t ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId GROUP BY a.AlbumId, a.Title ORDER BY SUM(t.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1;

WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS yr, SUM(Total) AS revenue
  FROM music_Invoice
  GROUP BY yr
)
SELECT yr AS year,
       revenue,
       ROUND((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY yr)) * 100.0 / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY yr), 1) AS yoy_pct_change
FROM yearly
ORDER BY yr;
WITH cust AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spent FROM music_Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_average FROM cust WHERE spent > (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM cust);
rows.note: Assumption: spend is the sum of `music_Invoice.Total` per customer, the average is taken across customers with at least one invoice, and customers with no invoices are excluded.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT p.PlaylistId, p.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS artist_count
  FROM music_Playlist p
  JOIN music_PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
  JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN music_Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
)
SELECT Name, artist_count
FROM counts
WHERE artist_count = (SELECT MAX(artist_count) FROM counts);
rows.note: I'll count distinct artists per playlist through the track → album → artist links, and return every playlist that ties for the maximum.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM music_InvoiceLine il JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) AS multi;
rows.note: I'm counting invoices whose line items include tracks from two or more distinct genres, using `music_InvoiceLine` joined to `music_Track` on `GenreId`.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS support_rep, SUM(i.Total) AS revenue_2010 FROM music_Invoice i JOIN music_Customer c ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId JOIN music_Employee e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId WHERE i.InvoiceDate >= '2010-01-01' AND i.InvoiceDate < '2011-01-01' GROUP BY e.EmployeeId ORDER BY revenue_2010 DESC LIMIT 1;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS discontinued_products FROM shop_Products WHERE Discontinued = '1';
SELECT CompanyName FROM shop_Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany';
rows.note: I'm assuming the Country column stores the value 'Germany' exactly.

rows.sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS product_count FROM shop_Categories c JOIN shop_Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName HAVING COUNT(p.ProductID) = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM shop_Products GROUP BY CategoryID))
SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS order_year, COUNT(*) AS num_orders FROM shop_Orders GROUP BY order_year ORDER BY order_year;

SELECT s.CompanyName AS shipper_name, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS avg_freight FROM shop_Orders o JOIN shop_Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assuming "freight cost per shipper" means the average of Freight in shop_Orders grouped by the shipper (ShipVia → shop_Shippers.CompanyName).

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM shop_Employees e WHERE e.ReportsTo = (SELECT EmployeeID FROM shop_Employees WHERE FirstName = 'Andrew' AND LastName = 'Fuller')
rows.note: I'm assuming Andrew Fuller is the employee with FirstName 'Andrew' and LastName 'Fuller' in shop_Employees, and that "report directly" means ReportsTo points to his EmployeeID.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM shop_Orders o
JOIN shop_Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2021-01-01'
GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, full_name
HAVING COUNT(*) = (
  SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM shop_Orders o2
    WHERE o2.OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND o2.OrderDate < '2021-01-01'
    GROUP BY o2.EmployeeID
  )
)
rows.note: I'm counting orders by `OrderDate` in calendar year 2020, and I'll return all employees tied for the top count.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM shop_Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM shop_Products);
rows.note: Assumption: "average product unit price" is the plain average of UnitPrice across all rows in shop_Products.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_shipped_to_france FROM shop_Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France' AND ShippedDate IS NOT NULL;
rows.note: I'm counting orders with `ShipCountry = 'France'` and a non-null `ShippedDate`, so undelivered orders are excluded.

rows.sql: SELECT p.ProductName AS product_name, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS revenue FROM "shop_Order Details" od JOIN shop_Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) DESC LIMIT 5;

SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice FROM shop_Products p JOIN shop_Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE p.UnitPrice = (SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM shop_Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) ORDER BY c.CategoryName

SELECT c.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue FROM shop_Orders o JOIN shop_Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID JOIN "shop_Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assuming revenue = sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over order lines whose OrderDate falls in 2021.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM shop_Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY month HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM shop_Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY strftime('%m', OrderDate)))
rows.note: I'm assuming "orders" means rows in `shop_Orders` by `OrderDate`, and I'll return all months tied for the top count.

rows.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(*) AS orders_1997 FROM shop_Orders o JOIN shop_Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '1997-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '1998-01-01' GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName) SELECT EmployeeID, FirstName, LastName, orders_1997 FROM counts WHERE orders_1997 = (SELECT MAX(orders_1997) FROM counts);
rows.note: The shop_Orders table has no orders from 1997. Its OrderDate range runs from 2012-07-10 to 2023-10-28, so the question can't be answered from this data.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_shipped_orders FROM shop_Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate;
SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days_to_ship FROM shop_Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND OrderDate IS NOT NULL;
rows.note: I'll treat "shipped orders" as rows with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and compute the average of the difference between ShippedDate and OrderDate in days.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM shop_Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel;
rows.note: Assumption: "still sold" means Discontinued = '0', and "below reorder level" means UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel.

rows.sql:
SELECT c.Country, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS order_count
FROM shop_Orders o
JOIN shop_Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2019'
GROUP BY c.Country
ORDER BY order_count DESC
LIMIT 1;

SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS beverages_pct_2023 FROM "shop_Order Details" od JOIN shop_Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN shop_Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN shop_Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2023';
rows.note: I'm treating revenue as UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over order lines dated in 2023, and the percentage as Beverages revenue divided by total 2023 revenue.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_with_orders_every_month_2020
FROM (
  SELECT CustomerID
  FROM shop_Orders
  WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2020'
  GROUP BY CustomerID
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12
) t;
rows.note: I'll count customers whose orders in 2020 cover all 12 calendar months, using `OrderDate`.

rows.sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID, SUM(d.UnitPrice * d.Quantity * (1 - d.Discount)) AS total
  FROM shop_Orders o
  JOIN "shop_Order Details" d ON d.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, AVG(t.total) AS avg_order_value
FROM order_totals t
JOIN shop_Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = t.EmployeeID
GROUP BY e.EmployeeID
ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC
LIMIT 1;

WITH supplier_rev AS (
  SELECT s.CompanyName AS company_name,
         SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM "shop_Order Details" od
  JOIN shop_Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  JOIN shop_Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
  JOIN shop_Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018'
  GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName
)
SELECT company_name, revenue
FROM supplier_rev
WHERE revenue = (SELECT MAX(revenue) FROM supplier_rev);
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue per line is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), filtered to orders dated in 2018.
